{{Short description|Salt associated with Easter in Russia}}
[[File:Четверговая_соль.jpg|thumb]]
'''Thursday salt''' is a dark salt produced in the [[Kostroma]] region, Russia. It is associated with Russian Orthodox Easter traditions, and was historically produced at the [[Trinity Lavra of St. Sergius]] monastery on [[Maundy Thursday]].<ref name="Slow Food Foundation">{{Cite web |title=Kostroma Black Salt - Arca del Gusto |url=https://www.fondazioneslowfood.com/en/ark-of-taste-slow-food/black-salt-from-kostroma/ |access-date=2023-10-28 |website=Slow Food Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="obliznis.ru">{{Cite web |title=What is thursday salt? How to prepare and use it? Magical use of Thursday salt. The forgotten taste of black salt. long history |url=https://obliznis.ru/en/chto-takoe-chetvergovaya-sol-kak-ee-gotovit-i-ispolzovat-magicheskoe.html |access-date=2023-11-03 |website=obliznis.ru}}</ref>

The salt is created by mixing [[rock salt]] with flavourings such as [[kvass]], herbs, or rye, and baking the mixture at a very high temperature for several hours. The process reduces the sodium chloride content and increases the content of other minerals such as calcium and potassium.<ref name="obliznis.ru" /><ref name="Slow Food Foundation" />
